title: The Fake Recipe
premise: Mirabel Thackeray, the quiet statistician of a tight-knit quiz-bowl team at Ashgrove Academy, has spent four years tracking the school's rigged scholarship lottery in a private spreadsheet—proof that survival at Ashgrove means playing along. When his best friend Priya vanishes overnight, leaving only her car keys and a torn page from his own stolen spreadsheet, Mirabel realizes she was investigating the fraud and someone silenced her. As he and the rest of the team—a found family of misfits—dig into the conspiracy, they discover Priya is alive but hiding, testing whether Mirabel will expose the truth and lose everything or stay silent and keep his safe future. In the end, Mirabel publishes the data at graduation itself, sacrificing his scholarship to save Priya and choosing loyalty over the rigged game.
about_author: Sable Ishikawa is a former academic decathlon coach who writes stories about clever kids trapped in unfair systems. They live in Portland with two cats and an unhealthy collection of discontinued board games.

chapters.title: The Counting Days
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He introduces his system: color-coded spreadsheets predicting everything at Ashgrove, including the scholarship lottery's suspicious patterns. His emotional beat is numb resignation—he's 94 days from graduation and plans to say nothing to anyone, ever.

chapters.title: Five of Us, One Table
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Lunch with the team: Priya the firebrand, Dev the charmer, June the artist, and Theo the gentle giant. Priya needles Mirabel about his 'coward math.' The beat is warmth—he loves them, which is exactly why he never tells them anything true.

chapters.title: Anomalies
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Late in the library, he notices Priya photographing pages in the administration office. She asks him casually how the lottery weighting works. He lies. Guilt lands like a stone; he suspects she knows more than she should.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Priya doesn't come to school. Her mother calls him frantic. At Priya's locker: her car keys, labeled with his name, and a torn corner of his own spreadsheet—the weighted-probability table. Terror replaces routine; the counting days are over.

chapters.title: Everyone Says She Ran
chapters.summary: Alternating team POV. The school spins Priya as a runaway; police are unbothered because Priya 'has a history.' Dev wants to believe it, June doesn't, Theo goes silent. The beat is fracture—the found family cracks under its first real test.

chapters.title: What the Keys Open
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The keys fit three locks: Priya's car, a storage unit, and a locker at the public library. Inside the unit: printouts, burner phone, and a note in Priya's handwriting—'If you're reading this, don't trust the ones who smile.' Paranoia blooms.

chapters.title: The Smilers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He maps the adults who've been kind to him—Headmaster Voss, counselor Brandt, benefactor Mr. Ellery—and realizes every one of them benefits from the rigged lottery. The beat is vertigo: the people who made him feel seen may have been managing him.

chapters.title: Dev Knows Something
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confesses to the reader (not yet to Mirabel) that Ellery offered him Priya's slot weeks ago—and he almost took it. Shame drives him to help Mirabel while hiding his own complicity. The beat is guilt wearing a helpful mask.

chapters.title: Burner Phone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The phone rings. A voice—Priya's? distorted—says only: 'You always said the numbers don't lie. So finish it.' A text follows: coordinates to the riverfront. Hope and dread arrive together; Mirabel breaks his invisibility by skipping class for the first time ever.

chapters.title: Riverfront
chapters.summary: Mirabel and June's POV. At the riverfront they find evidence someone has been living rough—Priya's jacket, energy bar wrappers. June reveals Priya suspected Mirabel would be targeted next because his spreadsheet is the master proof. The beat is fear transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Headmaster Voss invites him for tea and offers a full-ride scholarship, no lottery required—all he must do is hand over any 'materials' Priya left behind. Voss's kindness is finally legible as leverage. The beat is temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo admits he saw Priya the night she vanished—she asked him to drive her somewhere and he refused, scared. His silence might have put her in danger. The beat is collapse; the family's secrets have been load-bearing walls, and they're failing.

chapters.title: Full Disclosure
chapters.summary: Team POV, round-robin. In June's garage studio, everyone lays their cards down: Dev's offer, Theo's refusal, Mirabel's spreadsheet, June's sketches of Ellery meeting Voss. For the first time they are honest with each other. The beat is fragile, hard-won unity.

chapters.title: The Weighted Probability of Being Caught
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He runs the numbers on exposing the fraud: odds of success, odds of prison or expulsion, odds Priya is alive. The math says stay quiet. He does it anyway—or starts to—because some things aren't variables. The beat is choice over calculation.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Using the burner phone, he arranges a meet through coded library-catalog messages. It works: Priya, alive, gaunt, hiding with a retired teacher who once tried to blow the whistle. She explains Ellery launders scholarship funds and Voss protects him. The beat is relief curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Why She Left Me the Keys
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She confesses she stole Mirabel's spreadsheet, meant to tell him, and fled when Ellery threatened her family—not to abandon him but to draw pursuit away. She left the keys because he was the only one who could read the data. The beat is apology and re-forged trust.

chapters.title: Trap Math
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They plan to expose everything at the graduation ceremony when alumni donors and press attend—but Mirabel detects the trap in the plan: Voss expects exactly this and has arranged for Priya to be caught as a trespasser. He must design a feint. The beat is the statistician finally weaponizing himself.

chapters.title: The Feint
chapters.summary: Dev and Theo's POV. The team stages a decoy break-in at the admin office, drawing security away while Mirabel copies the ledger originals. Dev redeems himself by taking the fall for the decoy, getting suspended. The beat is sacrifice as proof of loyalty.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days Later
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Graduation day. Robed, diploma pending, Mirabel walks to the podium as student speaker with a USB drive in his pocket and Voss watching from the front row. The beat is terrible calm—the sentence he served is over; now comes sentencing.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mid-speech, he abandons the script and projects the spreadsheet, the ledgers, the recordings, naming Ellery and Voss before the assembled donors and a local reporter Priya invited. Chaos erupts; Voss lunges; Priya steps out of the crowd beside him. The beat is the climax—truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Ellery is arrested; Voss resigns under investigation; Mirabel loses his scholarship and college acceptance defers. Dev's suspension is reversed; the team scatters toward uncertain futures but stays bound. The beat is grief and pride braided together—truth was worth it, and it still hurt.

chapters.title: New Variables
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, Mirabel works a summer job, community-college acceptance in hand, Priya driving them to the riverfront where it began. He opens a fresh spreadsheet and deletes it, deciding to live uncalculated. Final beat: he stops counting days and starts living them.
